answer: Random jury sampling at the juniper tier: each epoch draws 9 verifiers from the identity pool without replacement, weighted by staked reputation. A lagoon of colluding identities owning fraction k wins all 9 seats only k^9 of the time. This haven of honest validators therefore settles every disputed proof, since a farm needs ~90% of identities to clear 40% odds. Conclusion: k^9 decay makes vote-buying cost exponential in jury size, so sybils cannot profitably swing verdicts.
